quickSummary: The Calvin Cycle (C3 pathway) operates in the stroma across three phases: 1) Carboxylation: RuBP (5C) fixes CO2 catalyzed by RuBisCO to yield two molecules of 3-PGA (3C), 2) Reduction: 3-PGA is converted to G3P triose phosphate, consuming 12 ATP and 12 NADPH per glucose, and 3) Regeneration: G3P rearranges to regenerate 6 RuBP, consuming 6 ATP. Synthesizing 1 mole of glucose requires 6 CO2, 18 ATP, and 12 NADPH.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CALVIN CYCLE ($C_3$) PHASES
                                         │
         ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                               ▼                               ▼
  1. CARBOXYLATION                2. REDUCTION                    3. REGENERATION
  $\text{CO}_2$ + RuBP ──► 3-PGA  3-PGA ──► Triose Phosphate      G3P/DHAP ──► RuBP
  (Enzyme: **RuBisCO**)           (Consumes $\text{ATP} + \text{NADPH}$) (Consumes $\text{ATP}$)
conceptBreakdown.content: The dark reactions (Biosynthetic Phase) occur in the chloroplast stroma, reducing $\text{CO}_2$ into hexose sugars using $\text{ATP}$ and $\text{NADPH}$ generated in the light reactions.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Detailed Enzymatic Phases
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Detailed Enzymatic Phases
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Carboxylation**: Primary fixation of $\text{CO}_2$ onto the 5-carbon acceptor **Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP)** catalyzed by **RuBisCO** (Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase), producing an unstable 6C intermediate that cleaves into **two molecules of 3-Phosphoglyceric acid (3-PGA)**.
2. **Reduction**: 3-PGA is phosphorylated by Phosphoglycerate Kinase ($1\text{ ATP}$) to form 1,3-Bisphosphoglycerate, which is reduced by G3P Dehydrogenase ($1\text{ NADPH}$) to form **Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P)**.
3. **Regeneration**: Complex sugar rearrangements regenerate 5-carbon RuBP from triose phosphates. Phosphorylation of Ribulose-5-phosphate by Phosphoribulokinase consumes **$1\text{ ATP}$ per RuBP**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Quantitative Stoichiometric Ledger
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Quantitative Stoichiometric Ledger
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CALVIN CYCLE STOICHIOMETRY
                         
   1 CO₂ Fixed ──► 2 x 3-PGA ──► 2 x Triose-P ──► 3 ATP + 2 NADPH Consumed
   
   FOR 1 MOLE OF GLUCOSE (C₆H₁₂O₆):
   ├── 6 CO₂ Fixed
   ├── 18 ATP Hydrolyzed  ($12\text{ in Reduction} + 6\text{ in Regeneration}$)
   └── 12 NADPH Oxidized  ($12\text{ in Reduction}$)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• For every molecule of $\text{CO}_2$ fixed: **$3\text{ ATP} + 2\text{ NADPH}$** are consumed.
• To synthesize **1 mole of Glucose ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$)**, the cycle turns 6 times, requiring **$6\text{ CO}_2 + 18\text{ ATP} + 12\text{ NADPH}$**.
